_confirmed_on_vehicle: 2026-09-15, ignition on, engine off, stationary, odometer 118904 km. byte_base 0 verified three ways: 2BC gave engine 24.75C and air 24.75C (cold engine sits at ambient) with gear = N; 2D0 gave ambient 24C from a different sensor; and the odometer appears twice, at 3F8 D1-D3 and 3FF D5-D7, both reading 118904. byte_base 1 gives a 138C air temperature on the same frame.

noise._: Payload bytes that free-run and must not count as a frame change. Bit N mutes byte N. Without these an ID republishes at its full cyclic rate for a whole ride and buries the real events.
noise._3FF: D2-D4 is a seconds counter. Measured on the bike incrementing by exactly 1 every 1000ms. The sheet documents it for the S1000R and its contributor could not find a use for it either. D1 (ambient light) and D5-D7 (odometer) stay live.
noise._2BC: D3-D4 is a 16-bit accumulator that only runs with the engine. Measured at idle climbing about 100 counts every 300ms, strictly monotonic, and it froze the instant the ignition went off. Purpose unknown (engine revolutions, run time or fuel used are all plausible) and it is in no published decode table. It made 2BC the noisiest ID on the bus by a wide margin: 347 raw publishes from 3857 frames, 9%, versus 1% for everything else. D2 (engine temperature) is deliberately NOT masked, so real temperature changes still publish. The current value stays visible in /can/ids and on the 60s heartbeat.
noise._2AC: D0 steps through a fixed sequence and D1's low nibble counts 0-E, per the sheet's S1000R column; this frame is otherwise undecoded and arrives every 99ms. Provisional: unmute it if D0/D1 turn out to carry state on the K25.

_byte_base: Dn is data[n]. The source table is the community BMW Motorrad CAN sheet, whose Key tab defines the payload as D0..D7; its 2013 ancestor numbered the same fields byte1..byte8, and the K25 Arduino sniffer built from that ancestor reads heated grips from data[7] and throttle from data[1], which is D7 and D1 here. Set to 1 only for a table written with D1 meaning data[0].
_sources: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1tUrOES5fQZa92Robr6uP8v2dzQDq9ohHjUiTU3isqdc (BMW Motorrad CAN messages, Keith Conger et al.)
https://github.com/4G-Gregg/BMW-GS-CAN-Sniffer (2010 R1200GS, Arduino; Event_Printer.ino is the ground truth for what actually ran on a K25)
_extraction: bytes[] is little-endian, least-significant first: (D3*256+D2) is bytes:[2,3]. nibble is 'high' or 'low'. value = raw*scale + offset. map keys are uppercase hex of the extracted value; 'default' labels any code not in the map, otherwise it reports as unmapped_0xNN. deadband/min_ms suppress chatter on analog signals.

signals.name: clutch_kill
signals._note: UNRESOLVED. Sheet says high nibble of D4, the Arduino sniffer reads the low nibble, same 6/A values. On the bike D4 read 0x16 (high 1, low 6) with the ignition on and engine off: the LOW nibble is the one holding 6 = clutch_out, which favours the sniffer. Pull the clutch, mark it, and see which nibble moves.

signals.name: side_stand
signals._note: UNRESOLVED. Read 0xE9 on the bike, so the high nibble was E, matching neither 5 nor 9. D5 is the only byte of 10C that moved during the whole capture, so the state does live here. Mark 'sidestand down', flip it, mark 'sidestand up', and diff.

signals.name: asc_abs
signals._note: UNRESOLVED. Sheet and sniffer agree on the low nibble of D5, but the bike read 9 there, matching neither 5 nor 6. Same D5 investigation as side_stand.

signals.name: throttle_pct
signals._note: The current sheet says D6(High Nibble) with a /255 formula. The 2013 sheet listed this as whole byte 7 (D6) with the same formula and the K50 row uses a whole byte too; the nibble label is a later transcription slip. Whole byte used. Should track throttle_valve_pct.

signals.name: high_beam
signals._note: Confirmed by the Arduino sniffer: LO_NIBBLE(data[6]), 9 on / A off.

signals.name: turn_signals
signals._note: Confirmed by the Arduino sniffer: whole data[7].

signals.name: abs
signals._note: UNRESOLVED. Sheet says low nibble of D1, the Arduino sniffer reads the high nibble, same 5/B values. On the bike D1 read 0x5F: the HIGH nibble holds 5 = on, which favours the sniffer, and ABS being on with the ignition on is right. D1 is the only byte of 294 that moved. Cycle ABS off, mark it, and confirm.

signals.name: front_wheel_speed_kmh
signals._note: The ~0.06 dates from the original 2013 entry and was never firmed up. No GPS needed: at steady speed in a straight line front and rear must agree, so scale = 0.06 * rear_raw / front_raw. Adjust here once measured.

signals.name: brake_levers
signals._note: Two encodings: static values (03/07/0B/0F) and, after two full wheel revolutions, in-motion values (00/04/08/0C). Both folded into one map since the values do not collide. The Arduino sniffer reads the low nibble with 3/7/B, which is the same thing.

signals.name: engine_temp_c
signals._note: deadband must exceed one quantisation step (scale), or a sensor resting between two codes reports forever. Observed on the bike dithering 0x40/0x41 = 24.0/24.8 C, which cleared the old 0.5 deadband every time. 1.0 swallows one step and still reports two.

signals.name: gear
signals._note: The 2013 sheet said the LOW nibble; the current sheet says HIGH, attributed to eight models including the K25, and assigns the low nibble to an oil-level fault flag. High nibble used.

signals.name: air_temp_c
signals._note: Same 0.75 quantum as engine_temp_c, so the same deadband rule applies.

signals.name: esa_preload
signals._note: Read C on the bike, which is 'Not Displayed' in the sheet's F800GT column, i.e. no ESA on this machine. Mapped to not_fitted rather than left unmapped. esa_damping likewise reads B,F which is outside its map.

signals.name: info_button
signals._note: Confirmed by the Arduino sniffer: LO_NIBBLE(data[5]), 5 short / 6 long.

signals.name: heated_grips
signals._note: Confirmed by the Arduino sniffer: HI_NIBBLE(data[7]), C/D/E. F is the whole-byte FF the ZFE sends with the ignition off, so it is labelled rather than reported as unmapped.

signals.name: ignition
signals._note: The sheet's FF=Off/DF=On row was contributed for the K25 and F800GSA and its 'DF' is simply the grips-low value with a fixed low nibble; it does not contradict heated_grips, it observed the same byte with the grips on low. Encoded as: FF means off, any other value means on.

signals.name: rdc_rear_bar
signals._note: Both bytes read FF on this bike, i.e. no RDC senders fitted. Without the invalid sentinel that publishes a confident and fictional 5.10 bar.

signals.name: ambient_light
signals._note: Sheet: B dark, 7 light, 3 and F unknown. The Arduino sniffer used 7 dark, 3 light. Read 9 on the bike in daylight with the ignition on, so neither source is right yet. Unmapped codes surface as unmapped_0xN; record what it sends in the dark and in sunlight.

signals.name: odometer_km_alt
signals._note: Second odometer copy. Confirmed on the bike: both this and 3F8 odometer_km read 118904.

signals.name: countdown
signals._note: Source lists no formula. Raw byte, published for identification.
